text:
Aisha: hey team, day 2 here. My M1 Pro dev machine is being finnicky I followed the dev-setup doc but running into python toolchain and docker issues. hoping for a quick checklist.
Rob: welcome! main things: install Xcode CLT, Homebrew for arm64 (/opt/homebrew), and make sure your shell init files load brew early. what errors are you seeing?
Aisha: python flakes in poetry env creation: "python: command not found" even though pyenv lists 3.10.8 as global. `pyenv which python` returns path inside ~/.pyenv but `python -V` is still system 2.7.
Sofia: sounds like pyenv isn't shimming correctly. do you have `eval "$(pyenv init --path)"` in ~/.zprofile and `eval "$(pyenv init -)"` in ~/.zshrc? on mac, the PATH order matters so shims come before /usr/bin.
Aisha: I had `export PATH="~/.pyenv/shims:$PATH"` in zshrc but not the eval lines. added them and restarted terminal, now python picks up. thanks.
Rob: another gotcha: if you installed python via brew before pyenv, you might have an /opt/homebrew/bin/python3 shadowing. `which -a python3` helps.
Aisha: fixed. now docker: docker desktop fails to start with "cannot allocate memory" when launching dev container. docker says it's using rosetta?
Sofia: for apple silicon ensure Docker Desktop is the Apple Silicon build. If you've installed an intel image previously, Docker may try to emulate with Rosetta and be slow. Also increase resources in Docker prefs (CPU/RAM). For compose projects, try `docker compose up --build --no-deps`.
Aisha: got the arm64 Docker Desktop, but my devcontainer in VS Code still uses an x86 base image and fails on binary installs. how to force arm images?
Rob: in devcontainer.json add `platform: "linux/arm64"` to the build or use multi-arch images. Example: `build: { "platform": "linux/arm64", "dockerfile": "Dockerfile" }`. Also set `remoteEnv.PATH` so host brew in devcontainer shell resolves things: `"remoteEnv": { "PATH": "/opt/homebrew/bin:${containerEnv:PATH}" }`
Aisha: sweet. last oddity: `asdf` and `pyenv` both in play for node/python. any tips for mixing?
Sofia: try to pick one for a runtime family: asdf can manage many runtimes (node, ruby, python) with plugins, which reduces overlap. If you keep pyenv, ensure you don't have duplicate shims in PATH. Keep `.tool-versions` authoritative if you use asdf.
Aisha: got it. side question: git asks for credentials each push inside devcontainer; host git credential helper works locally but not in container.
Rob: enable credential forwarding or mount the host git config/credential socket into the container. Alternatively install `git-credential-manager-core` in the container and configure 1password CLI or gcloud auth accordingly. For key forwarding, enable ssh agent in the container config: `"mounts": ["source=/run/host-services/ssh-auth.sock,target=/ssh-agent,type=bind"]` and set `"remoteEnv": { "SSH_AUTH_SOCK": "/ssh-agent" }`.
Aisha: im on 1Password for SSH and it shows the key in the menubar but container can't access it. i'll try the ssh-agent socket mount.
Sofia: one more: if you use `direnv`, ensure you don't auto-run heavy init in `.envrc` (like `asdf install --skip-existing`) on every cd. Use a script that is idempotent and fast.
Aisha: thanks all, this got me unstuck. infra bots: any links to internal guides?
Infra Bot: Hi Aisha  here are useful internal pages: https://intranet.redwood/company/onboarding/dev-setup, https://intranet.redwood/devcontainers-guides, and our `dotfiles` repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/dotfiles.
DevEx Bot: Tip: run our bootstrap script `curl -fsSL https://get.redwood.dev/bootstrap | bash` to install common tools, then open a deck issue in #devex if anything fails.
Aisha: will run the bootstrap and ping if anything else breaks. Appreciate the speedy help! :raised_hands:
